comments.author: Eric Speake
comments.message:
Using the grok-patterns file from the gist I get the following error on all of my logstash servers:

Received an event that has a different character encoding than you configured. {:text=>"\\u0000/\\u00005\\xC0\\u0011\\xC0\\u0012\\xC0\\u0013\\xC0\\u0014\\u0001\\u0000\\u0000\\e\\u0000\\u0005\\u0000\\u0005\\u0001\\u0000\\u0000\\u0000\\u0000\\u0000", :expected_charset=>"UTF-8", :level=>:warn}

I have looked to be sure it wasn't an issue with the ssl certificate. But when I changed the grok-patterns file on a server that had been working I received the same error. I am still looking further at the SSL as a possible gotcha.

replies.author: Eric Speake
replies.message: This did turn out to be a certificate issue and has been resolved.

comments.author: Poluvex Tripplex
comments.message: Would it not be a bit easier to simply use logstash-forwarder (lumberjack) to ship your logs to logstash instead? It does allow for adding fields and taging at source, adds encryption and would only require one input stream.

replies.author: LanyonM
replies.message:
Hi Poluvex,
Logstash-forwarder is a great option as well. It's how we ship logs in our monitoring pipeline at work, so I can attest to its suitability. Given this post's age, I hope it serves more as an explanation of the connection between log4j conversion patterns and grok parser patterns.

It's also on my list to experiment with circumventing the on-disk logs entirely via socket appenders.

comments.author: Roger Welin
comments.message: This is way too much work and ugly log parsing that burns CPU. A much better alternative would be to set up the tomcat container to log json from the beginning, with for example logstash-logback encoder, and just send the logs using logbacks TCP or UDP appender. No ugly parsing, logshipping etc.
